newsitem.title: ITALY: Rate cut expectations recede in Italy money market.
newsitem.headline: Rate cut expectations recede in Italy money market.

text.p: Italy's money market has pushed further out expectations for an interest rate cut with the implicit overnight rate seen higher than a week ago, a study by the Bocconi University research arm Igier showed on Friday.

The implicit overnight rate in one month is seen standing at 7.51 percent, just over Italy's 7.50 percent official discount rate, and from an actual market level of 8.00 percent Thursday, the day on which Igier based its study.
One week ago the implicit overnight rate was seen standing at 7.43 percent. One month ago it was seen at 7.41 percent.
On a three month timeframe, the implicit overnight rate is seen at 6.79 percent, from 6.75 percent a week ago and 7.26 percent one month ago.
On a one-year timeframe the implicit overnight rate is seen standing at 6.02 percent from 5.86 percent a week ago and 7.26 percent last month.
On a one year horizon, the implicit overnight rate is seen at 6.02 percent from 5.86 percent seen a week ago and 6.25 percent one month ago.

The spread between the implicit Italian overnight rate and the implicit German overnight rate, considered a good indicator of market confidence in Europe's economic and monetary union, rose to 207 basis points from 180 bps one week ago and 202 bps two weeks ago. One month ago this differential was at 181 bps.
